title: Minneapolis Mayor vetoes new robotaxi rules
key_facts: Minneapolis Mayor Jacob Frey vetoed an ordinance requiring human monitors in the driver's seat of robotaxis
The 'Workers Drive Minneapolis' policy would have covered Waymo, Tesla Cybercab and Zoox
Frey said requiring a driver in a driverless car does not make sense
Rideshare workers spoke against robotaxis at a council meeting earlier in the week
The city council needs nine votes to override the veto
quote_evidence: Minneapolis' Mayor has vetoed a new ordinance that would require human monitors in the driver's seat of robotaxis.
The city council will need nine votes to override the mayor's veto.
why_it_matters_hint: A city is deciding whether robotaxis can operate without a human in the driver's seat.
notes: Short local TV report carrying NBC text; the veto date is not stated and Frey's statement is paraphrased.
